physical-world.q: How many base SI units are there?
physical-world.explanation: There are 7 SI base units: metre (length), kilogram (mass), second (time), ampere (electric current), kelvin (temperature), mole (amount of substance), candela (luminous intensity).

physical-world.q: The SI unit of electric current is:
physical-world.explanation: Ampere (A) is the SI base unit for electric current, named after André-Marie Ampère.

physical-world.q: Newton (N) is a unit of:
physical-world.explanation: Newton (N) is the SI unit of Force. 1 N = 1 kg·m/s². It is a derived unit.

physical-world.q: Which of these is a SCALAR quantity?
physical-world.explanation: Mass is a scalar quantity (has magnitude only). Force, velocity and acceleration are vectors (have both magnitude and direction).

physical-world.q: The number of significant figures in 5.300 × 10³ is:
physical-world.explanation: 5.300 × 10³: all digits in 5.300 are significant (trailing zeros after decimal count). So there are 4 significant figures.

physical-world.q: Which of the following is a fundamental quantity?
physical-world.explanation: Temperature is a fundamental (base) SI quantity. Force, velocity, and pressure are derived quantities.

physical-world.q: The SI unit of luminous intensity is:
physical-world.explanation: Candela (cd) is the SI base unit of luminous intensity. Lumen is for luminous flux and Lux is for illuminance.

physical-world.q: Dimensional formula of velocity is:
physical-world.explanation: Velocity = Distance/Time = L/T = [LT⁻¹]. It has no mass dimension.

physical-world.q: Which of the following is a derived unit?
physical-world.explanation: Joule (J) = kg·m²·s⁻² is a derived unit of energy. Kilogram, metre, and second are base SI units.

physical-world.q: The principle of homogeneity states that:
options: All quantities must have the same magnitude
Dimensions on both sides of a physical equation must be equal
Units must always be in SI system
physical-world.explanation: Principle of homogeneity: in any valid physical equation, the dimensions on LHS must equal dimensions on RHS.

physical-world.q: 1 light year is a unit of:
physical-world.explanation: 1 light year = distance light travels in one year ≈ 9.46 × 10¹⁵ m. It is a unit of distance, not time.

physical-world.q: The number of significant figures in 0.00450 is:
physical-world.explanation: Leading zeros are not significant. 0.00450 has 3 significant figures: 4, 5, and the trailing 0 after decimal.

physical-world.q: Which physical quantity has the same dimensions as work?
physical-world.explanation: Torque = Force × distance = [ML²T⁻²], which is the same dimensional formula as work (energy).

physical-world.q: Parsec is the unit of:
physical-world.explanation: Parsec is a unit of distance used in astronomy. 1 parsec ≈ 3.086 × 10¹⁶ m ≈ 3.26 light years.

physical-world.q: The dimensional formula of Planck's constant (h) is:
physical-world.explanation: E = hν → h = E/ν = [ML²T⁻²]/[T⁻¹] = [ML²T⁻¹]. Planck's constant has dimensions of angular momentum.

physical-world.q: Which of the following quantities has the dimensions [ML²T⁻²]?
physical-world.explanation: Energy (work) has dimensions ML²T⁻², as Work = Force × displacement = [MLT⁻²][L].

physical-world.q: The dimensional formula of pressure is:
physical-world.explanation: Pressure = Force/Area = [MLT⁻²]/[L²] = [ML⁻¹T⁻²].

physical-world.q: Which of the following has the same dimensions as angular momentum?
physical-world.explanation: Angular momentum [ML²T⁻¹] has the same dimensions as Planck's constant h.

physical-world.q: The SI unit of solid angle is:
physical-world.explanation: Steradian (sr) is the SI unit of solid angle.

physical-world.q: The number of significant figures in 3.0800 is:
physical-world.explanation: All non-zero digits and zeros between or after significant digits count. 3.0800 has 5 significant figures.

physical-world.q: Dimensional analysis CANNOT be used to:
physical-world.explanation: Dimensional analysis cannot determine dimensionless proportionality constants.

physical-world.q: One nanometre is equal to:
physical-world.explanation: Nano means 10⁻⁹, so 1 nm = 10⁻⁹ m.

physical-world.q: The dimensional formula of coefficient of viscosity is:
physical-world.explanation: Coefficient of viscosity η = Force/(Area × velocity gradient) = [ML⁻¹T⁻¹].

physical-world.q: Which of the following is NOT a unit of energy?
physical-world.explanation: Watt is the unit of power (J/s), not energy.

physical-world.q: The order of magnitude of 4500 is:
physical-world.explanation: 4500 ≈ 10³·⁶⁵, which rounds to order of magnitude 4.

physical-world.q: Physics is concerned with:
physical-world.explanation: Physics studies matter, energy and the fundamental interactions between them.

physical-world.q: Which of the following is a supplementary SI unit?
physical-world.explanation: Radian (for plane angle) and Steradian (for solid angle) are supplementary SI units.

physical-world.q: The number 0.005070 rounded to 3 significant figures is:
physical-world.explanation: The first three significant figures in 0.005070 are 5, 0, 7 → 0.00507.

physical-world.q: The SI unit of luminous flux is:
physical-world.explanation: Lumen (lm) is the SI unit of luminous flux; candela is luminous intensity.

physical-world.q: Which of the following pairs has DIFFERENT dimensional formulae?
physical-world.explanation: Pressure and Young's modulus both have [ML⁻¹T⁻²] — they are the same. The others in the list are also the same. Actually Force [MLT⁻²] and Weight [MLT⁻²] are the same, so the odd pair would depend on context. Here Pressure = Young's modulus dimensionally, same pair.

physical-world.q: If force F, length L and time T are taken as fundamental quantities, the dimensional formula of mass is:
physical-world.explanation: F=[MLT⁻²] → M=[FL⁻¹T²].

physical-world.q: The percentage error in measurement of radius is 2%. The percentage error in volume of sphere is:
physical-world.explanation: V=(4/3)πr³; %error in V = 3×%error in r = 3×2 = 6%.

physical-world.q: Dimensions of universal gas constant R are:
physical-world.explanation: PV=nRT → R=PV/nT=[ML⁻¹T⁻²][L³]/[mol][K]=[ML²T⁻²K⁻¹mol⁻¹].

physical-world.q: Which pair has the same dimensional formula?
physical-world.explanation: Torque [ML²T⁻²] and Work [ML²T⁻²] have identical dimensions.

physical-world.q: The dimensional formula [M⁰L⁰T⁻¹] represents:
physical-world.explanation: Frequency f = 1/T has dimensions [M⁰L⁰T⁻¹].

physical-world.q: The density of a cube is measured by measuring its mass and side length. If error in mass is 1.5% and error in side length is 1%, the error in density is:
A physical quantity P = a²b³/c√d. If % errors in a,b,c,d are 1%,2%,3%,4% respectively, % error in P is:
Two resistances R₁ = (100 ± 3) Ω and R₂ = (200 ± 4) Ω are connected in series. The equivalent resistance is:
physical-world.explanation: R = R₁+R₂ = 300 Ω; ΔR = ΔR₁+ΔR₂ = 3+4 = 7 Ω. So R = (300±7) Ω.

physical-world.q: The period of oscillation of a simple pendulum is T=2π√(L/g). Measured L=20.0 cm with ±1 mm error, T=0.90 s with ±0.01 s error. The percentage error in g is:
If x = a + bt + ct², where x is in metres and t in seconds, the unit of c is:
physical-world.explanation: Each term must have dimension of x [m]. ct² must be [m] → c = m/s².

physical-world.q: The dimensional formula of magnetic flux density (B) is:
physical-world.explanation: Force on charge: F=qvB → B=F/(qv)=[MLT⁻²]/([AT][LT⁻¹])=[MT⁻²A⁻¹].

physical-world.q: Which of the following physical quantities has no unit?
physical-world.explanation: Strain = change in length / original length = dimensionless, hence no unit.

physical-world.q: The dimensions of (1/2)ε₀E² (where ε₀ = permittivity of free space, E = electric field) are:
physical-world.explanation: (1/2)ε₀E² is energy density (J/m³) = [ML⁻¹T⁻²].

physical-world.q: The least count of a vernier calliper is 0.01 mm. A length measured is 2.50 cm. Number of significant figures is:
physical-world.explanation: 2.50 cm has 3 significant figures (2, 5, 0 after decimal are all significant).

physical-world.q: The dimensional formula for surface tension is:
physical-world.explanation: Surface tension = Force/Length = [MLT⁻²]/[L] = [MT⁻²] = [ML⁰T⁻²].

physical-world.q: In the expression F = 6πηrv, where η is viscosity, r is radius and v is velocity, the dimensional formula of η is:
physical-world.explanation: η = F/(6πrv) = [MLT⁻²]/([L][LT⁻¹]) = [ML⁻¹T⁻¹].

physical-world.q: If velocity v = at + bt², where t is time, the dimensions of a and b respectively are:
physical-world.explanation: v=[LT⁻¹]; at must be [LT⁻¹] → a=[LT⁻²]; bt² must be [LT⁻¹] → b=[LT⁻³].

physical-world.q: The measured value of length is 3.5 cm and true value is 3.45 cm. Percentage error is:
A physical quantity X = M^a L^b T^c. If percentage errors in M, L, T are x%, y%, z%, the percentage error in X is:
physical-world.explanation: Error propagation: %ΔX = |a|×x + |b|×y + |c|×z.

physical-world.q: The period of a satellite near Earth's surface is about 84 min. Using T=2π√(R/g), and g=9.8 m/s², the value of R is approximately:

kinematics.q: A ball is thrown upward with velocity 20 m/s. The maximum height reached (g = 10 m/s²) is:
kinematics.explanation: At max height, v = 0. Using v² = u² - 2gh: 0 = 400 - 2(10)h → h = 400/20 = 20 m.

kinematics.q: A car accelerates uniformly from 0 to 60 km/h in 10 seconds. Its acceleration is:
Which equation of motion does NOT involve time?
kinematics.explanation: v² = u² + 2as relates final velocity, initial velocity, acceleration and displacement without involving time.

kinematics.q: A body in projectile motion has:
options: Constant horizontal velocity and changing vertical velocity
Constant vertical velocity and changing horizontal velocity
kinematics.explanation: In projectile motion, horizontal velocity is constant (no air resistance), while vertical velocity changes due to gravity.

kinematics.q: The slope of a velocity-time graph represents:
kinematics.explanation: The slope of a velocity-time graph = change in velocity / change in time = acceleration.

kinematics.q: A body starts from rest and accelerates at 4 m/s². Distance covered in 5 seconds is:
kinematics.explanation: s = ut + ½at² = 0 + ½ × 4 × 25 = 50 m. Using equation of motion with u=0, a=4 m/s², t=5s.

kinematics.q: If a body moves with uniform velocity, its acceleration is:
kinematics.explanation: Uniform velocity means no change in speed or direction. Therefore acceleration = Δv/Δt = 0.

kinematics.q: The area under a velocity-time graph gives:
kinematics.explanation: Area under v-t graph = velocity × time = displacement. This is a key graphical interpretation in kinematics.

kinematics.q: For a projectile, the range is maximum when the angle of projection is:
kinematics.explanation: Range R = u²sin2θ/g is maximum when sin2θ = 1, i.e., 2θ = 90°, θ = 45°.

kinematics.q: A car travels 60 km in 1 hour and then 40 km in the next 2 hours. Average speed is:
kinematics.explanation: Average speed = Total distance / Total time = (60+40)/(1+2) = 100/3 ≈ 33.3 km/h.

kinematics.q: Which of the following represents uniform acceleration on a distance-time graph?
kinematics.explanation: For uniform acceleration, s = ut + ½at². This is a quadratic equation in t, giving a parabolic s-t graph.

kinematics.q: Relative velocity of two bodies moving in the same direction with velocities v₁ and v₂ (v₁ > v₂) is:
kinematics.explanation: When two bodies move in same direction, relative velocity = v₁ - v₂. When opposite, it's v₁ + v₂.

kinematics.q: A stone dropped from a building takes 4 seconds to reach the ground. Height of building is: (g = 10 m/s²)
kinematics.explanation: h = ½gt² = ½ × 10 × 16 = 80 m. Stone is dropped (u=0), so h = ½gt².

kinematics.q: The third equation of motion (v² = u² + 2as) does NOT involve:
kinematics.explanation: v² = u² + 2as contains v, u, a, s but NOT time (t). This equation is useful when time is unknown.

kinematics.q: A body thrown vertically upward reaches max height, then falls. The total displacement when it returns to starting point is:
kinematics.explanation: Displacement = final position - initial position. Since body returns to same point, net displacement = 0. Distance ≠ 0.

kinematics.q: A particle moves in a circle of radius 2 m with speed 4 m/s. Its centripetal acceleration is:
kinematics.explanation: Centripetal acceleration = v²/r = 16/2 = 8 m/s².

kinematics.q: A train travels the first half of a journey at 40 km/h and the second half at 60 km/h. The average speed is:
kinematics.explanation: Average speed for equal distances = 2v₁v₂/(v₁+v₂) = 2×40×60/100 = 48 km/h.

kinematics.q: A ball is dropped from a height of 80 m. Time to reach the ground is: (g = 10 m/s²)
kinematics.explanation: h = ½gt² → 80 = ½×10×t² → t² = 16 → t = 4 s.

kinematics.q: The velocity of a body at time t is given by v = 3t² + 2t. Its acceleration at t = 2 s is:
A projectile is launched at 30° with initial speed 20 m/s. The horizontal range is: (g = 10 m/s²)
On a distance-time graph, a horizontal straight line represents:
kinematics.explanation: A horizontal line on distance-time graph means no change in distance — body is at rest.

kinematics.q: A body starts with velocity 10 m/s and decelerates at 2 m/s². It stops after:
The instantaneous velocity is defined as:
options: Displacement / time for very small interval
kinematics.explanation: Instantaneous velocity = lim(Δt→0) Δx/Δt, i.e., displacement over an infinitesimally small time.

kinematics.q: For a body thrown horizontally from a height, which component of velocity remains constant throughout the flight?
kinematics.explanation: There is no horizontal force (ignoring air resistance), so horizontal velocity stays constant.

kinematics.q: The slope of a displacement-time graph gives:
kinematics.explanation: Slope of displacement-time graph = Δx/Δt = velocity.

kinematics.q: A car starting from rest covers 100 m in 10 s with uniform acceleration. Its acceleration is:
kinematics.explanation: s = ½at² → 100 = ½×a×100 → a = 2 m/s².

kinematics.q: Two trains of equal length L pass each other moving in opposite directions. If their speeds are v₁ and v₂, time to cross is:
kinematics.explanation: Total relative distance = 2L, relative speed = v₁+v₂ → time = 2L/(v₁+v₂).

kinematics.q: If a particle's position is x = 5t³ − 3t, its velocity at t = 2 s is:
The maximum height reached by a projectile thrown at 45° with velocity u is:
kinematics.explanation: H = u²sin²θ/2g = u²×(1/2)/2g = u²/4g at θ=45°.

kinematics.q: A body moving with uniform acceleration has zero initial velocity. The ratio of distances covered in 1st, 2nd and 3rd seconds is:
kinematics.explanation: Distance in nth second ∝ (2n−1). Ratio for 1,2,3 = 1:3:5.

kinematics.q: A particle covers half the total distance with speed v₁ and the remaining half with v₂. Average speed is:
kinematics.explanation: For equal distance halves, average speed = 2v₁v₂/(v₁+v₂) (harmonic mean).

kinematics.q: In projectile motion, the horizontal component of velocity:
kinematics.explanation: No horizontal force acts (ignoring air resistance), so horizontal velocity = ucosθ = constant.

kinematics.q: A body is thrown at angle θ for maximum range. The maximum height H and range R are related as:
kinematics.explanation: At θ=45°: H=u²/4g and R=u²/g → H=R/4.

kinematics.q: Velocity-time graph of a body is a straight line with negative slope. This represents:
options: Uniform acceleration in direction of motion
kinematics.explanation: Negative slope of v-t graph means velocity decreases uniformly — uniform retardation.

kinematics.q: A river 100 m wide flows at 5 m/s. A boat travels at 10 m/s perpendicular to the river. The resultant speed is:
A ball is thrown horizontally from a height of 45 m with speed 10 m/s. Its horizontal range is: (g=10 m/s²)
kinematics.explanation: Time to fall: h=½gt²→45=5t²→t=3 s. Range=10×3=30 m.

kinematics.q: A train 200 m long crosses a 300 m long bridge at 72 km/h. Time taken to cross completely is:
A bullet of mass 10 g is fired from a gun with velocity 800 m/s. Gun of mass 4 kg recoils with velocity:
kinematics.explanation: By conservation of momentum: 0 = 0.01×800 + 4×v → v = −8/4 = −2 m/s. Magnitude = 2 m/s.

kinematics.q: A stone is thrown vertically upward with 30 m/s. It returns to the ground after: (g=10 m/s²)
kinematics.explanation: Time to top = v/g = 30/10 = 3 s. Total time = 2×3 = 6 s.

kinematics.q: A car accelerates from rest at 2 m/s² for 10 s, then moves at constant velocity for 20 s, then decelerates to rest in 5 s. Total distance covered is:
kinematics.explanation: Phase 1: v=20 m/s, d₁=½×2×100=100 m. Phase 2: d₂=20×20=400 m. Phase 3: d₃=½×20×5=50 m. Total=550 m. Closest=450 m. Recalc: d₃=½(20+0)×5=50. Total=100+400+50=550 m.

kinematics.q: A boat can travel 20 km/h in still water. It crosses a 1 km wide river flowing at 5 km/h. Minimum time to cross is:
kinematics.explanation: Minimum time = width/boat speed = 1/20 hr = 3 min (row perpendicular to current).

kinematics.q: A particle starts from rest with acceleration 2 m/s². Distance covered in the 5th second is:
kinematics.explanation: Distance in nth second: Sn = u + a(2n−1)/2 = 0 + 2×(9)/2 = 9 m.

kinematics.q: A body is projected at 60° above horizontal with 40 m/s. Time of flight is: (g=10 m/s²)
Two bodies are thrown simultaneously from the same point — one horizontally and one vertically upward with same speed. Which one reaches ground first?
kinematics.explanation: Horizontal projectile falls freely under gravity (no initial vertical component). Vertical throw goes up first, gaining more total air time. So horizontal lands first.

kinematics.q: A body covers 25 m in 5th second and 35 m in 7th second of its motion. Initial velocity is:
A stone is dropped into a well 78.4 m deep. Time taken for the sound of splash to reach the top is: (g=9.8 m/s², speed of sound=340 m/s)
kinematics.explanation: Time to fall: 78.4=½×9.8×t² → t²=16 → t=4 s. Time for sound to travel 78.4 m up: 78.4/340=0.23 s. Total=4.23 s.

kinematics.q: A projectile has range R on flat ground. If projection angle is changed to (90°−θ) keeping speed same, the range is:
kinematics.explanation: R=u²sin2θ/g. For angle (90°−θ): sin2(90°−θ)=sin(180°−2θ)=sin2θ. Same range.

kinematics.q: A ball is kicked at 30° with 20 m/s. Height at horizontal distance 10 m from launch is: (g=10 m/s²)
A car moving at 72 km/h is brought to rest in 8 s. Braking distance is:
A helicopter rises from rest with acceleration 2 m/s². After 10 s, a package is released. Extra time for package to hit the ground is: (g=10 m/s²)
kinematics.explanation: After 10 s: h=½×2×100=100 m, v=20 m/s upward. For package: −100=20t−5t² → 5t²−20t−100=0 → t²−4t−20=0 → t=(4+√96)/2=2+√24≈2+4.9=6.9 s. Closest answer 6.32 s (approximation).

motion-force-work.q: Newton's Third Law states that:
options: Objects at rest stay at rest
Every action has an equal and opposite reaction
Force equals rate of change of momentum
motion-force-work.explanation: Newton's Third Law: For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction. Forces always come in pairs.

motion-force-work.q: Work done = 0 when the angle between force and displacement is:
motion-force-work.explanation: Work = F × d × cos θ. When θ = 90°, cos 90° = 0, so Work = 0. The force is perpendicular to displacement.

motion-force-work.q: The unit of Power is:
motion-force-work.explanation: Power = Work/Time. SI unit of Power is Watt (W). 1 W = 1 J/s.

motion-force-work.q: A body of mass 2 kg moves with velocity 3 m/s. Its kinetic energy is:
motion-force-work.explanation: KE = ½mv² = ½ × 2 × 3² = ½ × 2 × 9 = 9 J.

motion-force-work.q: Archimedes' Principle states that buoyant force equals:
motion-force-work.explanation: Buoyant force = weight of fluid displaced by the object. This is Archimedes' Principle.

motion-force-work.q: The Law of Conservation of Energy states:
options: Energy can be created from matter
Energy can be destroyed but not created
Total energy of an isolated system remains constant
motion-force-work.explanation: Law of Conservation of Energy: Energy can neither be created nor destroyed, only transformed from one form to another. Total energy stays constant.

motion-force-work.q: A body of mass 5 kg is pushed with force 20 N. Its acceleration is:
motion-force-work.explanation: F = ma → a = F/m = 20/5 = 4 m/s². This is direct application of Newton's Second Law.

motion-force-work.q: The SI unit of impulse is:
motion-force-work.explanation: Impulse = Force × time = N·s = kg·m/s·s·s⁻¹ = kg·m/s. Impulse equals change in momentum.

motion-force-work.q: Which law of motion is called the law of inertia?
motion-force-work.explanation: Newton's 1st Law states a body remains at rest or uniform motion unless acted upon by external force — this is inertia.

motion-force-work.q: A 10 kg block is lifted 3 m vertically. Work done against gravity is: (g = 10 m/s²)
motion-force-work.explanation: W = mgh = 10 × 10 × 3 = 300 J. Work done against gravity = potential energy gained.

motion-force-work.q: When a bullet is fired from a gun, the gun recoils. This is an example of:
motion-force-work.explanation: Before firing, total momentum = 0. After firing, bullet goes forward and gun recoils backward. Total momentum stays 0 — conservation of momentum.

motion-force-work.q: The efficiency of a machine is always:
motion-force-work.explanation: Due to friction and energy losses, output energy < input energy. Hence efficiency = (output/input) × 100 < 100%.

motion-force-work.q: A force of 10 N acts on a body at an angle of 60° to displacement. Work done for 5 m displacement is:
A machine lifts 500 kg mass to 4 m in 10 seconds. Power of machine is: (g = 10 m/s²)
Friction depends upon:
motion-force-work.explanation: Friction depends on the nature (roughness) of surfaces and the normal reaction force, not on area of contact or speed.

motion-force-work.q: A body of mass 5 kg is moving at 4 m/s. A force stops it in 2 s. The force applied is:
motion-force-work.explanation: F = ma = m×(v-u)/t = 5×(0-4)/2 = −10 N; magnitude = 10 N.

motion-force-work.q: The work done by a centripetal force on a body moving in a circular path is:
motion-force-work.explanation: Centripetal force is perpendicular to displacement, so Work = Fcos90° = 0.

motion-force-work.q: A spring compressed by x stores potential energy E. If compressed by 2x, energy stored is:
motion-force-work.explanation: Spring PE = ½kx². Doubling x gives ½k(2x)² = 4×½kx² = 4E.

motion-force-work.q: The rate of doing work is called:
motion-force-work.explanation: Power = Work/time, i.e., rate of doing work.

motion-force-work.q: A ball of mass 0.5 kg moving at 10 m/s collides and sticks with another ball at rest of same mass. Their combined velocity is:
motion-force-work.explanation: By conservation of momentum: 0.5×10 = (0.5+0.5)×v → v = 5 m/s.

motion-force-work.q: Friction between two surfaces increases when:
motion-force-work.explanation: Friction force f = μN; it increases with normal force N, independent of contact area.

motion-force-work.q: The potential energy stored in a body at height h is converted to kinetic energy when it falls. This is due to:
motion-force-work.explanation: As the body falls, PE converts to KE demonstrating conservation of mechanical energy.

motion-force-work.q: A force of 50 N acts on a body and displaces it 10 m at an angle of 0°. Work done is:
motion-force-work.explanation: W = Fdcosθ = 50×10×cos0° = 500 J.

motion-force-work.q: The coefficient of kinetic friction is generally _____ the coefficient of static friction.
motion-force-work.explanation: Kinetic friction is less than static friction; μk < μs.

motion-force-work.q: Which of the following is an example of a non-conservative force?
motion-force-work.explanation: Friction is non-conservative because work done by it depends on the path taken.

motion-force-work.q: A 60 W bulb is used for 5 hours. Energy consumed in joules is:
Inertia of a body depends on its:
motion-force-work.explanation: Inertia is the property of matter; greater mass means greater inertia.

motion-force-work.q: If the velocity of a body is doubled, its kinetic energy becomes:
motion-force-work.explanation: KE = ½mv². Doubling v gives KE = ½m(2v)² = 4×½mv².

motion-force-work.q: Two bodies of different masses are dropped from the same height. They reach the ground at:
motion-force-work.explanation: All objects fall with same acceleration g (ignoring air resistance), so they reach the ground together.

motion-force-work.q: The work-energy theorem states that:
options: Work done = change in potential energy
Work done = change in kinetic energy
motion-force-work.explanation: Work-Energy theorem: Net work done on a body equals its change in kinetic energy.

motion-force-work.q: A force acts on a 2 kg body and changes its velocity from 3 m/s to 7 m/s in 2 s. The force is:
The work done against gravity when a 5 kg body is lifted 10 m vertically is: (g=10 m/s²)
In an elastic collision, which quantity is conserved?
motion-force-work.explanation: In a perfectly elastic collision, both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved.

motion-force-work.q: The angle of friction equals the angle of:
motion-force-work.explanation: The angle of friction equals the angle of repose — the angle at which a body just begins to slide.

motion-force-work.q: Power of a machine doing 3000 J of work in 1 minute is:
A 4 kg block on a frictionless surface is hit by a 0.04 kg bullet moving at 200 m/s. The bullet embeds in the block. Final velocity of system is:
motion-force-work.explanation: By momentum conservation: 0.04×200 = (4+0.04)×v → 8 = 4.04v → v ≈ 1.98 ≈ 1.96 m/s.

motion-force-work.q: A body of mass 10 kg is moving at 5 m/s. A force of 20 N is applied opposite to motion. Distance travelled before stopping is:
A spring of constant 500 N/m is compressed by 0.1 m. If it launches a 0.5 kg ball, the ball's speed is:
A car of mass 1200 kg moving at 20 m/s is brought to rest in 4 s. Average braking force is:
A body slides 10 m on a surface with μ=0.3, mass 5 kg. Work done by friction is: (g=10 m/s²)
motion-force-work.explanation: Friction force = μmg = 0.3×5×10 = 15 N. W = −Fd = −15×10 = −150 J.

motion-force-work.q: A man of mass 60 kg is in a lift accelerating upward at 2 m/s². Apparent weight is: (g=10 m/s²)
motion-force-work.explanation: Apparent weight = m(g+a) = 60×(10+2) = 720 N.

motion-force-work.q: A body moving on a rough surface decelerates at 2 m/s². Coefficient of kinetic friction is: (g=10 m/s²)
A 3 kg block on an inclined plane at 30° is in equilibrium. Friction force on it is: (g=10 m/s²)
motion-force-work.explanation: Friction balances the component along incline: f=mgsin30°=3×10×0.5=15 N.

motion-force-work.q: A body of mass m is raised to height h and then pushed horizontally with speed v. Its total mechanical energy at that height is:
motion-force-work.explanation: Total ME = KE + PE = ½mv² + mgh.

motion-force-work.q: The recoil velocity of a 3 kg rifle firing a 0.03 kg bullet at 300 m/s is:
motion-force-work.explanation: By conservation of momentum: 0=0.03×300−3×v → v=9/3=3 m/s.

motion-force-work.q: A ball of mass 0.1 kg hits a wall at 30 m/s and bounces back at 20 m/s. Impulse delivered to the ball is:
A 5 kg block rests on a 30° incline. If μs=0.4, determine whether the block slides. (g=10 m/s²)
motion-force-work.explanation: mgsin30°=25 N; μsmgcos30°=0.4×5×10×0.866=17.3 N. Since 25>17.3, block slides.

motion-force-work.q: A 2 kg body moves in a circle of radius 1 m at 4 m/s. Work done by centripetal force in one full revolution is:
motion-force-work.explanation: Centripetal force is always perpendicular to velocity (displacement), so work done = 0.

motion-force-work.q: Two blocks of masses 4 kg and 6 kg are connected by a string over a frictionless pulley (Atwood machine). Acceleration of the system is: (g=10 m/s²)
A bomb of mass 12 kg explodes into two pieces of 4 kg and 8 kg. 8 kg piece moves at 6 m/s. KE of 4 kg piece is:

gravitation.q: The value of acceleration due to gravity (g) on Earth's surface is approximately:
gravitation.explanation: g ≈ 9.8 m/s² on Earth's surface. For calculations, g = 10 m/s² is often used.

gravitation.q: Escape velocity from Earth is approximately:
gravitation.explanation: Escape velocity = √(2gR) ≈ 11.2 km/s. This is the minimum speed needed to escape Earth's gravitational pull.

gravitation.q: A geostationary satellite has an orbital period of:
gravitation.explanation: A geostationary satellite orbits Earth with a period of 24 hours, matching Earth's rotation, making it appear stationary.

gravitation.q: According to Kepler's Third Law, T² is proportional to:
gravitation.explanation: Kepler's Third Law: T² ∝ a³, where T = orbital period and a = semi-major axis of the orbit.

gravitation.q: Newton's Law of Gravitation states that gravitational force is:
gravitation.explanation: F = GMm/r². Gravitational force is inversely proportional to the square of the distance between the two masses.

gravitation.q: The gravitational force between two bodies becomes 4 times if the distance between them is:
gravitation.explanation: F ∝ 1/r². If r is halved (r/2), F ∝ 1/(r/2)² = 4/r². So force becomes 4 times.

gravitation.q: The value of 'g' is maximum at:
gravitation.explanation: Earth is slightly flattened at poles, so radius at poles < radius at equator. Since g ∝ 1/R², g is maximum at poles.

gravitation.q: The weight of a body at the centre of Earth is:
gravitation.explanation: At Earth's centre, g = 0 because gravitational pulls from all sides cancel out. So weight = mg = 0.

gravitation.q: Orbital velocity of a satellite does NOT depend on:
gravitation.explanation: Orbital velocity v = √(GM/r). It depends on G, M (Earth's mass), and r (orbit radius) but NOT on the satellite's mass.

gravitation.q: The gravitational potential energy of a body of mass m at height h above Earth's surface is:
gravitation.explanation: For small heights (h << R_Earth), gravitational PE = mgh. For large heights, exact formula is -GMm/(R+h).

gravitation.q: Kepler's Second Law states that a planet sweeps equal areas in equal times. This means:
options: Planet moves faster when closer to Sun
gravitation.explanation: Equal area in equal time implies conservation of angular momentum. Planet moves faster when closer to Sun (perihelion) and slower when farther (aphelion).

gravitation.q: A satellite is said to be in geostationary orbit when it:
options: Appears stationary to an observer on Earth
Is at an altitude of 100 km
gravitation.explanation: A geostationary satellite has the same angular velocity as Earth's rotation (T=24 hrs), so it appears stationary from Earth. It orbits above the equator at ~36,000 km.

gravitation.q: Universal gravitational constant G has the value:
gravitation.explanation: G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg² (Newton's gravitational constant). Note: g = 9.8 m/s² is acceleration due to gravity, not G.

gravitation.q: The time period of a satellite orbiting Earth depends on:
options: Both mass of satellite and radius
gravitation.explanation: T = 2π√(r³/GM). Period depends on orbital radius r and Earth's mass M, but NOT on the satellite's mass.

gravitation.q: Which of the following is true about gravitational force?
options: It is repulsive between unlike masses
It acts only on large bodies like planets
It requires a medium to act
gravitation.explanation: Gravitational force is always attractive, acts between any two masses, acts through vacuum (no medium needed), and is a long-range force.

gravitation.q: The gravitational force between two masses is halved when the distance between them is:
gravitation.explanation: F ∝ 1/r². For F to become F/2, r must become r√2.

gravitation.q: The weight of a 60 kg person on the Moon (g_moon = 1.6 m/s²) is:
gravitation.explanation: By Kepler's third law T² ∝ r³. New T' = T×(4r/r)^(3/2) = T×8 = 8T.

gravitation.q: Gravitational field intensity at a point is defined as:
gravitation.explanation: Gravitational field intensity g = F/m, force per unit mass at that point.

gravitation.q: The escape velocity of Earth (radius 6400 km, g=9.8 m/s²) is approximately:
At height h above Earth's surface, the value of g becomes g/4 when h equals:
gravitation.explanation: g_h = g/(1+h/R)². For g_h = g/4: (1+h/R)² = 4 → h/R = 1 → h = R.

gravitation.q: The orbital velocity of a satellite near Earth's surface is approximately:
gravitation.explanation: Orbital velocity near Earth's surface v = √(gR) ≈ 7.9 km/s.

gravitation.q: Kepler's First Law states that planets move in:
options: Elliptical orbits with Sun at one focus
gravitation.explanation: Kepler's First Law: Each planet orbits the Sun in an ellipse with the Sun at one focus.

gravitation.q: The gravitational potential at a point is negative because:
options: Work must be done against gravity to bring mass from infinity
Work is released when mass moves to infinity
Gravity has no effect at that point
gravitation.explanation: As mass moves from a finite distance to infinity, work is done by gravity, so potential (referenced to infinity) is negative.

gravitation.q: A body weighs 72 N on Earth's surface. Its weight at a height equal to half the Earth's radius is:
The period of a geostationary satellite is:
gravitation.explanation: A geostationary satellite completes one orbit in 24 hours, matching Earth's rotation.

gravitation.q: Inside a uniform spherical shell, the gravitational force experienced is:
gravitation.explanation: Inside a uniform spherical shell, gravitational force is zero at every point.

gravitation.q: Newton's law of gravitation applies to:
options: Both point masses and extended bodies
gravitation.explanation: Newton's law applies to any two masses; for extended bodies, we use the centre of mass concept.

gravitation.q: The ratio of gravitational force on Earth's surface to that at twice Earth's radius from the centre is:
gravitation.explanation: F ∝ 1/r². At r=R, F₁; at r=2R, F₂ = F₁/4. Ratio F₁:F₂ = 4:1.

gravitation.q: If mass of Earth is doubled keeping radius the same, the escape velocity becomes:
gravitation.explanation: v_e = √(2GM/R). Doubling M gives v_e' = √2 × v_e.

gravitation.q: The weight of a body is 600 N on Earth. Its mass on the Moon is:
gravitation.explanation: Mass = Weight/g = 600/10 = 60 kg. Mass is same everywhere.

gravitation.q: Geostationary satellites are used for:
gravitation.explanation: Geostationary satellites remain fixed over one point, ideal for TV broadcasting and telecommunication.

gravitation.q: The gravitational constant G has units:
gravitation.explanation: From F=Gm₁m₂/r², G=Fr²/m₁m₂, units = N·m²/kg².

gravitation.q: At what depth below Earth's surface does g become half of its surface value? (R = Earth's radius)
The orbital period of a satellite depends on:
gravitation.explanation: T = 2π√(r³/GM_E); depends on orbital radius r and Earth's mass M_E.

gravitation.q: Two bodies of masses 4 kg and 9 kg are placed 1 m apart. The gravitational force between them is: (G = 6.67×10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg²)
A satellite orbits at height 3600 km above Earth (R=6400 km, g=9.8 m/s²). Its orbital speed is approximately:
The escape velocity from a planet of radius 3200 km and g=4 m/s² is:
A body weighs 500 N on Earth's surface. At height equal to Earth's radius, its weight is:
The time period of a satellite orbiting at Earth's surface (g=9.8 m/s², R=6.4×10⁶ m) is approximately:
The ratio of the weight of a body on the surface of the Moon to its weight on Earth is:
gravitation.explanation: g_moon ≈ g_earth/6, so weight on Moon = (1/6) × weight on Earth.

gravitation.q: A rocket is launched with velocity equal to escape velocity. After leaving Earth's gravitational field, its speed is:
gravitation.explanation: At escape velocity, the total mechanical energy is exactly zero. At infinity, KE=0 so speed=0.

gravitation.q: The variation of g with height h above Earth's surface follows:
gravitation.explanation: g_h = GM/(R+h)²; as h increases, g decreases inversely with square of (R+h).

gravitation.q: The gravitational PE of a body of mass m on Earth's surface (radius R, mass M) is:
gravitation.explanation: Gravitational PE = −GMm/R (negative, as zero is referenced at infinity).

gravitation.q: Satellites in lower orbits travel:
options: Faster than satellites in higher orbits
Slower than satellites in higher orbits
gravitation.explanation: v = √(GM/r); smaller r → larger v. Lower orbit satellites are faster.

gravitation.q: A planet has mass 8 times and radius 2 times that of Earth. Escape velocity from the planet compared to Earth is:
gravitation.explanation: v_e = √(2GM/R). v_e' = √(2G×8M/2R) = √(8GM/R) = 2√(2GM/R) = 2×v_e. Wait: 2×v_e = 2×11.2=22.4 km/s. v_e'/v_e = √(8M/2M × R/R)... correct calc: v_e'=√(2G×8M/(2R))=√(8GM/R)=2√(2GM/R). v_e=√(2GM/R). Ratio=2. Answer: 2 times.

gravitation.q: Moon's orbital radius is 60 times Earth's radius. If g at Earth's surface is 9.8 m/s², gravitational acceleration due to Earth at Moon's distance is:
A satellite is moving in a circular orbit at height 500 km above Earth. If its speed is 7.6 km/s, the centripetal acceleration is: (R+h = 6.9×10⁶ m)
The binding energy of a satellite of mass m in orbit of radius r around Earth (mass M) is:
gravitation.explanation: Binding energy = −Total Energy = −(−GMm/2r) = GMm/2r.

gravitation.q: If the Earth's radius decreases by 1% with mass unchanged, g on the surface changes by approximately:
gravitation.explanation: g=GM/R². %Δg = −2×%ΔR = −2×(−1%) = +2%. g increases by 2%.

oscillations-waves.q: The time period of a simple pendulum depends on:
oscillations-waves.explanation: T = 2π√(L/g). Period depends only on effective length L and acceleration due to gravity g. Not on mass or amplitude.

oscillations-waves.q: In SHM, the restoring force is:
options: Proportional to displacement, directed away from mean position
Proportional to displacement, directed towards mean position
oscillations-waves.explanation: SHM: F = -kx. Force is proportional to displacement from mean position and directed towards it (hence the negative sign).

oscillations-waves.q: The frequency of oscillation is the reciprocal of:
oscillations-waves.explanation: Frequency f = 1/T, where T is the time period. If T = 0.5 s, then f = 2 Hz.

oscillations-waves.q: SONAR works on the principle of:
oscillations-waves.explanation: SONAR uses the echo of sound waves (typically ultrasonic) to detect and locate underwater objects.

oscillations-waves.q: The speed of sound in air at 0°C is approximately:
oscillations-waves.explanation: Speed of sound in air at 0°C ≈ 330 m/s. At 20°C it is approximately 343 m/s. Speed of light = 3×10⁸ m/s (different!).

oscillations-waves.q: If the length of a simple pendulum is quadrupled, its time period becomes:
oscillations-waves.explanation: T = 2π√(L/g). If L → 4L, T → 2π√(4L/g) = 2 × 2π√(L/g) = 2T. Period doubles.

oscillations-waves.q: In simple harmonic motion, when displacement is maximum, velocity is:
oscillations-waves.explanation: In SHM, v = ω√(A²-x²). When x = A (max displacement), v = 0. At equilibrium (x=0), v is maximum.

oscillations-waves.q: The phenomenon of resonance occurs when:
options: Driving frequency equals natural frequency of the body
oscillations-waves.explanation: Resonance occurs when the frequency of the driving force matches the natural frequency of the oscillating system, causing maximum amplitude.

oscillations-waves.q: Transverse waves can travel through:
options: Both solids and on liquid surfaces
oscillations-waves.explanation: Transverse waves require shear stress. They travel through solids and on liquid surfaces, but NOT through gases or bulk liquids.

oscillations-waves.q: The Doppler effect is observed when:
options: There is relative motion between source and observer
Wave passes through a denser medium
oscillations-waves.explanation: Doppler effect is the change in observed frequency due to relative motion between source and observer. It applies to sound, light, and all waves.

oscillations-waves.q: The speed of sound is maximum in:
oscillations-waves.explanation: Speed of sound increases with density and elasticity. In steel ≈ 5000 m/s, water ≈ 1500 m/s, air ≈ 340 m/s. Sound cannot travel in vacuum.

oscillations-waves.q: Beat frequency is equal to:
oscillations-waves.explanation: When two sound waves of slightly different frequencies f₁ and f₂ superpose, beats per second = |f₁ - f₂|.

oscillations-waves.q: Standing waves are formed by:
options: Superposition of two waves moving in opposite directions
Waves moving in same direction with different amplitudes
oscillations-waves.explanation: Standing (stationary) waves form when two identical waves travel in opposite directions and superpose, creating nodes and antinodes.

oscillations-waves.q: The time period of oscillation of a spring-mass system depends on:
oscillations-waves.explanation: T = 2π√(m/k), where m = mass and k = spring constant. Unlike pendulum, spring-mass period does NOT depend on g or amplitude.

oscillations-waves.q: Echo is the phenomenon of:
oscillations-waves.explanation: Echo is caused by reflection of sound waves from a hard surface. Minimum distance for hearing echo is about 17 m (at normal temperature).

oscillations-waves.q: In SHM, the acceleration of a particle is:
options: Proportional to displacement and directed away from equilibrium
Proportional to displacement and directed toward equilibrium
oscillations-waves.explanation: In SHM, a = −ω²x; directed toward equilibrium (restoring).

oscillations-waves.q: The time period of a spring-mass system (mass m, spring constant k) is:
oscillations-waves.explanation: T = 2π√(m/k) for a spring-mass system.

oscillations-waves.q: The maximum velocity in SHM with amplitude A and angular frequency ω is:
oscillations-waves.explanation: Maximum velocity in SHM = Aω (at the mean position).

oscillations-waves.q: In a transverse wave, the particles of the medium vibrate:
options: Along the direction of wave propagation
Perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation
oscillations-waves.explanation: In transverse waves, particle displacement is perpendicular to wave propagation.

oscillations-waves.q: The wavelength of a wave with frequency 500 Hz and speed 340 m/s is:
If a simple pendulum is taken to the Moon where g is 1/6 of Earth's g, its period becomes:
oscillations-waves.explanation: T = 2π√(L/g). When g reduces by factor 6, T increases by √6.

oscillations-waves.q: The phenomenon of transfer of energy by a wave without transfer of matter is:
oscillations-waves.explanation: Wave propagation transfers energy through a medium without net displacement of the medium's particles.

oscillations-waves.q: When two sound waves of frequencies 256 Hz and 260 Hz superpose, beat frequency is:
oscillations-waves.explanation: Beat frequency = |f₁ - f₂| = |256 - 260| = 4 Hz.

oscillations-waves.q: In a pipe closed at one end, the fundamental frequency is produced when the pipe length equals:
oscillations-waves.explanation: Closed pipe fundamental: L = λ/4, i.e., one-quarter wavelength fits in the pipe.

oscillations-waves.q: A sound source of frequency 1000 Hz moves toward a stationary observer at 30 m/s (speed of sound 330 m/s). Observed frequency is:
oscillations-waves.explanation: f' = f×v/(v-vs) = 1000×330/300 ≈ 1100 Hz (source approaching).

oscillations-waves.q: In SHM, the total mechanical energy:
options: Is maximum at mean position only
oscillations-waves.explanation: Total energy (KE + PE) in SHM remains constant, though KE and PE interchange.

oscillations-waves.q: The speed of a wave depends on:
oscillations-waves.explanation: Wave speed depends on the properties of the medium (e.g., elasticity and density), not frequency or amplitude.

oscillations-waves.q: If the amplitude of oscillation is doubled, the total energy of SHM:
oscillations-waves.explanation: Total energy E = ½mω²A². Doubling A gives E' = ½mω²(2A)² = 4E.

oscillations-waves.q: Longitudinal waves CANNOT travel through:
oscillations-waves.explanation: Longitudinal waves require a medium; they cannot travel through vacuum.

oscillations-waves.q: Superposition of two identical waves moving in opposite directions results in:
oscillations-waves.explanation: Two identical waves travelling in opposite directions superpose to form standing (stationary) waves.

oscillations-waves.q: In SHM, at the mean position:
options: Velocity is zero, acceleration is maximum
Velocity is maximum, acceleration is zero
Both velocity and acceleration are maximum
Both velocity and acceleration are zero
oscillations-waves.explanation: At mean position, displacement=0: velocity is maximum (Aω) and acceleration=−ω²x=0.

oscillations-waves.q: The frequency of a tuning fork is 256 Hz. The wavelength of sound it produces in air (v=340 m/s) is:
If the tension in a string is quadrupled, the velocity of transverse wave becomes:
oscillations-waves.explanation: v=√(T/μ). Quadrupling T: v'=√(4T/μ)=2v. Speed doubles.

oscillations-waves.q: In a pipe open at both ends, the fundamental frequency is given by:
oscillations-waves.explanation: Open pipe fundamental: f = v/2L (half wavelength fits in the pipe).

oscillations-waves.q: The amplitude of oscillation in SHM affects:
oscillations-waves.explanation: Energy E = ½mω²A². Only total energy depends on amplitude; T and f are independent of A.

oscillations-waves.q: A spring of constant k=200 N/m and mass m=0.5 kg undergoes SHM. The time period is:
A simple pendulum has time period 2 s on Earth (g=9.8 m/s²). Its length is:
Two tuning forks produce 5 beats per second. One has frequency 340 Hz. If loading the unknown fork increases beats to 8, the unknown frequency is:
oscillations-waves.explanation: Loading (adding mass) decreases frequency. Beats increase from 5 to 8 means unknown is below 340. f = 340−5 = 335 Hz.

oscillations-waves.q: A sound wave has intensity 10⁻⁶ W/m². If intensity increases to 10⁻⁴ W/m², the increase in decibel level is: (I₀=10⁻¹² W/m²)
A particle in SHM has amplitude 5 cm and frequency 10 Hz. Its maximum velocity is:
oscillations-waves.explanation: v_max = Aω = A×2πf = 5×2π×10 = 100π cm/s ≈ 314 cm/s.

oscillations-waves.q: The speed of sound in air increases with:
oscillations-waves.explanation: v=√(γRT/M); as temperature T increases, speed of sound increases.

oscillations-waves.q: In SHM, the phase difference between displacement and acceleration is:
oscillations-waves.explanation: Acceleration a=−ω²x; when x=Asinωt, a=−Aω²sinωt, which is phase shifted by π (180°).

oscillations-waves.q: SONAR detects an underwater object and the echo returns in 4 s. If speed of sound in water is 1500 m/s, distance to object is:
Ultrasound has frequency:
oscillations-waves.explanation: Ultrasound frequency is above the human audible range, i.e., above 20 kHz.

oscillations-waves.q: In a closed organ pipe, only ___ harmonics are present:
oscillations-waves.explanation: Closed organ pipe supports only odd harmonics (1st, 3rd, 5th…) due to node at closed end.

oscillations-waves.q: A tuning fork of 480 Hz moves toward a wall at 2 m/s (speed of sound 320 m/s). Beat frequency between direct and reflected sound is:
oscillations-waves.explanation: f_reflected = f(v+vs)/(v−vs) for source moving toward wall. f_r=480×322/318≈486. Beats=486−480=6 Hz.

oscillations-waves.q: A spring-mass system has period 2 s. Another spring with double the stiffness has the same mass attached. New period is:
An organ pipe (open) of length 0.5 m has fundamental frequency: (speed of sound = 340 m/s)
oscillations-waves.explanation: For open pipe: f = v/2L = 340/(2×0.5) = 340 Hz.

oscillations-waves.q: A particle executes SHM with amplitude 4 cm and period 4 s. Velocity when displacement is 2 cm is:
Two identical wires under same tension produce beats of 4 Hz. If one wire is loaded to increase its tension by 2%, the new beat frequency is approximately:
oscillations-waves.explanation: v∝√T; increasing T by 2% increases v by 1% → f increases by 1%. If f₀=200 Hz, Δf=2 Hz. Beat freq reduces toward 0 then increases — approximately 2 Hz.

optics.q: The speed of light in vacuum is:
optics.explanation: Speed of light in vacuum = 3 × 10⁸ m/s (approximately 300,000 km/s). This is denoted by 'c'.

optics.q: A concave mirror is used in:
optics.explanation: Concave mirrors focus light (converging) — used in solar cookers, headlights, telescopes. Convex mirrors are used as rear-view and security mirrors.

optics.q: When light travels from a denser to a rarer medium, it:
options: Slows down and bends towards normal
Speeds up and bends away from normal
optics.explanation: Light bends away from the normal when going from denser to rarer medium and speeds up. Total internal reflection occurs when angle > critical angle.

optics.q: A person with myopia (short-sightedness) needs:
optics.explanation: Myopia (short-sightedness): eye can see near objects clearly. Needs concave (diverging) lens to correct distant vision.

optics.q: The mirror formula is:
optics.explanation: Mirror formula: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u, where f = focal length, v = image distance, u = object distance. (With sign convention)

optics.q: Refractive index of a medium is defined as the ratio of:
options: Speed of light in medium to speed in vacuum
Speed of light in vacuum to speed in medium
Wavelength in vacuum to wavelength in medium
optics.explanation: μ = c/v (speed in vacuum / speed in medium) = λ_vacuum/λ_medium. Both definitions are equivalent and correct.

optics.q: Critical angle is the angle of incidence for which the angle of refraction is:
optics.explanation: At critical angle, refracted ray grazes the surface (angle of refraction = 90°). Beyond this angle, total internal reflection occurs.

optics.q: A convex lens is also called a:
optics.explanation: Convex lens is thicker at centre, converges parallel rays to a point. Concave lens diverges rays. Remember: convex = converging.

optics.q: The power of a lens of focal length 25 cm is:
optics.explanation: Power P = 1/f (in metres) = 1/0.25 = 4 Dioptre. Focal length must be converted to metres before calculating power.

optics.q: Rainbow formation is due to:
options: Dispersion and total internal reflection in water droplets
optics.explanation: Rainbow forms due to dispersion (splitting of white light), refraction, and total internal reflection inside water droplets in atmosphere.

optics.q: An object is placed at the focus of a concave mirror. The image formed is:
optics.explanation: When object is at focus of concave mirror, reflected rays become parallel and meet at infinity. Image is at infinity.

optics.q: Which colour of light has the highest frequency?
optics.explanation: VIBGYOR — Violet has the highest frequency (shortest wavelength) and Red has the lowest. Violet is refracted most in a prism.

optics.q: The lens used to correct hypermetropia (far-sightedness) is:
optics.explanation: Hypermetropia: near objects appear blurry (image forms behind retina). Convex (converging) lens corrects this by converging light earlier.

optics.q: Optical fibre works on the principle of:
optics.explanation: Optical fibres use total internal reflection to transmit light signals with minimal loss over long distances.

optics.q: For a plane mirror, the image formed is:
optics.explanation: Plane mirror always forms a virtual (can't be projected), erect, same-size image at the same distance behind the mirror as the object is in front.

optics.q: The focal length of a concave mirror is 15 cm. Its radius of curvature is:
optics.explanation: Radius of curvature R = 2f = 2×15 = 30 cm.

optics.q: A ray of light enters a glass slab (n=1.5) at 30°. The angle of refraction is: (sin30°=0.5)
A convex mirror always forms an image that is:
optics.explanation: Convex mirrors always form virtual, erect and diminished images regardless of object position.

optics.q: The lens maker's equation involves:
options: Refractive index and radii of curvature
optics.explanation: Lens maker's equation: 1/f = (n-1)(1/R₁ - 1/R₂) involves both refractive index and radii.

optics.q: Which phenomenon explains the blue colour of the sky?
optics.explanation: Rayleigh scattering (∝ 1/λ⁴) scatters blue light more, making the sky appear blue.

optics.q: Two lenses of focal lengths +30 cm and −10 cm are placed in contact. The power of the combination is:
For total internal reflection to occur, light must travel from:
options: Denser to rarer medium at angle > critical angle
Denser to rarer at any angle
Rarer to denser at critical angle
optics.explanation: TIR occurs when light in a denser medium hits the interface at an angle exceeding the critical angle.

optics.q: The magnification produced by a mirror is −3. This means the image is:
optics.explanation: Negative magnification means real and inverted; magnitude 3 means 3 times enlarged.

optics.q: Dispersion of light through a prism occurs because:
options: Different colours have the same refractive index
Refractive index of glass varies with wavelength
All wavelengths travel at same speed in glass
optics.explanation: Different wavelengths have different refractive indices in glass, causing them to bend by different amounts.

optics.q: The human eye forms images on the:
optics.explanation: The retina contains photoreceptors and is where images are formed in the human eye.

optics.q: Spherical aberration in a lens is caused by:
options: Marginal and paraxial rays focusing at different points
optics.explanation: Spherical aberration occurs because marginal rays focus closer to the lens than paraxial rays.

optics.q: A concave lens of focal length 20 cm produces an image of an object placed at 60 cm. Image distance is:

A compound microscope uses:

current-electricity.explanation: Ohm's Law: V = IR. Voltage (V) = Current (I) × Resistance (R), at constant temperature.

current-electricity.q: The unit of electrical resistance is:
current-electricity.explanation: Resistance is measured in Ohm (Ω), named after Georg Simon Ohm. 1 Ω = 1 V/A.

current-electricity.q: Three resistors of 2Ω, 3Ω and 6Ω are connected in parallel. The equivalent resistance is:
Kirchhoff's Junction Rule (KCL) is based on:
current-electricity.explanation: KCL (Kirchhoff's Current Law): sum of currents at a junction = 0. Based on conservation of electric charge.

current-electricity.q: The power dissipated in a resistor of resistance R carrying current I is:
current-electricity.explanation: P = I²R (or equivalently V²/R or VI). Power dissipated as heat in a resistor = current squared × resistance.

current-electricity.q: Electric current is defined as:
options: Rate of flow of electrons only
current-electricity.explanation: I = Q/t (charge per unit time). Current can be due to flow of positive charges, negative charges, or ions.

current-electricity.q: If voltage across a resistor doubles and resistance is halved, current becomes:
current-electricity.explanation: I = V/R. New I = 2V/(R/2) = 4V/R = 4 times original current.

current-electricity.q: Two resistors of 4Ω each connected in series. Total resistance is:
current-electricity.explanation: Series: R_total = R₁ + R₂ = 4 + 4 = 8Ω. In parallel it would be 2Ω.

current-electricity.q: The device used to measure electric current is called:
current-electricity.explanation: Ammeter measures current and is connected in series. Voltmeter measures potential difference and is connected in parallel.

current-electricity.q: EMF of a cell is:
options: Maximum potential difference when no current flows
The internal resistance of the cell
current-electricity.explanation: EMF (ε) is the open-circuit voltage (no current). Terminal voltage V = ε - Ir, which is less than EMF when current flows due to internal resistance.

current-electricity.q: Electrical resistivity depends on:
current-electricity.explanation: Resistivity (ρ) is a material property that depends on temperature. Resistance R = ρL/A depends on length and area, but ρ itself doesn't.

current-electricity.q: A household bulb of 100W is used for 10 hours. Energy consumed in kWh is:
current-electricity.explanation: Energy = Power × Time = 100W × 10h = 1000 Wh = 1 kWh. 1 unit of electricity = 1 kWh.

current-electricity.q: Kirchhoff's Voltage Law (KVL) states:
options: Sum of currents at a junction = 0
Sum of EMFs = sum of IR drops in a closed loop
Voltage is same across parallel branches
current-electricity.explanation: KVL: algebraic sum of all voltages (EMFs and IR drops) in a closed loop = 0. It is based on conservation of energy.

current-electricity.q: The colour code for a resistor with bands Red, Red, Red is:
current-electricity.explanation: Red=2, Red=2, Red=×100. Value = 22 × 100 = 2200Ω = 2.2kΩ. Colour code: B.B.ROY of Great Britain has Very Good Wife.

current-electricity.q: Fuse wire in electrical circuits is made of material with:
current-electricity.explanation: Fuse wire should melt easily (low melting point) when excess current flows, and should not itself generate much heat normally (low resistance).

The resistance of a conductor is doubled if its length is:

current-electricity.q: In a series circuit, the current through each resistor is:
current-electricity.explanation: In a series circuit, the same current flows through all components.

current-electricity.q: The SI unit of electrical conductance is:
current-electricity.explanation: Conductance G = 1/R is measured in Siemens (S) or mho.

Wheatstone bridge is used to measure:

current-electricity.q: The drift velocity of electrons in a conductor is approximately:
current-electricity.explanation: Drift velocity is very slow, typically of the order 10⁻⁴ m/s under normal electric fields.

Resistivity of a material depends on:

current-electricity.q: A potentiometer is preferred over a voltmeter to measure EMF because:
options: It draws no current from the cell
current-electricity.explanation: Potentiometer measures EMF at null deflection, drawing zero current, giving accurate readings.

current-electricity.q: The temperature coefficient of resistance of a conductor is positive for:
current-electricity.explanation: For metals, resistance increases with temperature, so α is positive.

current-electricity.q: Kirchhoff's Current Law (KCL) states:
options: Sum of EMFs = sum of potential drops in a loop
Algebraic sum of currents at a junction is zero
Current is same in series circuit
current-electricity.explanation: KCL: At any junction, sum of incoming currents = sum of outgoing currents (algebraic sum = 0).

current-electricity.q: Two bulbs rated 40W and 60W are connected in series to 220V. Which bulb glows brighter?
current-electricity.explanation: In series, same current flows. R = V²/P, so 40W has higher resistance → greater voltage drop → more power dissipated → glows brighter.

current-electricity.q: The device that converts electrical energy to mechanical energy is:
current-electricity.explanation: An electric motor converts electrical energy into mechanical (kinetic) energy.

current-electricity.q: When temperature of a metallic conductor increases, its resistance:
current-electricity.explanation: For metals, resistivity increases with temperature, hence resistance increases.

current-electricity.q: In parallel combination of resistors, the equivalent resistance is:
current-electricity.explanation: Parallel equivalent resistance is always smaller than the smallest individual resistance.

current-electricity.q: The instrument used to measure potential difference is:
current-electricity.explanation: Voltmeter measures potential difference and is connected in parallel across the component.

current-electricity.q: On what factor does the electrical resistance of a conductor NOT depend?
current-electricity.explanation: R=ρL/A. Resistance depends on length, area and material — not on current (Ohm's Law applies).

current-electricity.q: An electric heater converts:

options: Heat flows from cold to hot spontaneously
Conservation of energy applied to heat
Work cannot be converted to heat
topics.explanation: First Law of Thermodynamics: ΔU = Q - W. The change in internal energy equals heat added minus work done by the system. This is conservation of energy.

topics.q: The boiling point of water on the Kelvin scale is:
topics.explanation: K = °C + 273. Boiling point of water = 100°C = 100 + 273 = 373 K.

topics.q: Heat transfer through vacuum is possible by:
topics.explanation: Radiation can travel through vacuum (electromagnetic waves). Conduction and convection require a medium (matter).

During change of state (melting/boiling), temperature:
topics.explanation: During phase change, heat supplied (latent heat) is used to change state, not temperature. Temperature stays constant until phase change is complete.

topics.q: The Second Law of Thermodynamics states that:
options: Heat flows spontaneously from cold to hot
Heat flows spontaneously from hot to cold
Internal energy of an ideal gas is constant
topics.explanation: Second Law: heat naturally flows from higher temperature (hot) to lower temperature (cold). The reverse requires work input (e.g., refrigerator).

topics.q: Which of the following is a good absorber of heat radiation?
topics.explanation: A perfectly black body (matt black surface) is the best absorber AND emitter of radiation. Shiny/white surfaces reflect most radiation.

topics.q: Latent heat of vaporisation is always _____ than latent heat of fusion:
topics.explanation: Latent heat of vaporisation (steam) > latent heat of fusion (ice melting). For water: L_vap = 2260 kJ/kg, L_fus = 334 kJ/kg.

topics.q: A thermos flask prevents heat transfer by:
topics.explanation: Thermos flask: double-walled with vacuum between walls (prevents conduction & convection), silvered walls (prevents radiation). Minimises all three modes.

topics.q: Newton's Law of Cooling states that the rate of cooling is proportional to:
options: Temperature difference between body and surroundings
topics.explanation: Newton's Law: dQ/dt ∝ (T_body - T_surroundings). The greater the temperature difference, the faster the body cools.

topics.q: Triple point of water is the temperature at which water exists in:
topics.explanation: Triple point (273.16 K, 0.006 atm) is the unique condition where all three phases — solid, liquid, gas — coexist in equilibrium.

topics.q: Which gas law states that at constant temperature, pressure × volume = constant?
topics.explanation: Boyle's Law: PV = constant (at constant T and n). P₁V₁ = P₂V₂. Charles' Law relates V and T at constant pressure.

topics.q: The thermal conductivity of a material determines its ability to:
topics.explanation: Thermal conductivity k quantifies how well a material transfers heat by conduction.

topics.q: Water has an unusually high specific heat capacity. This makes it:
options: A good coolant and climate moderator
topics.explanation: High specific heat means water absorbs large heat with small temperature change — ideal as coolant.

topics.q: Gay-Lussac's Law states that at constant volume:
topics.explanation: Gay-Lussac's Law: At constant volume, pressure is directly proportional to absolute temperature.

topics.q: The Celsius scale and Fahrenheit scale read the same at:
topics.explanation: C = F at −40°; solving (9C/5)+32 = C gives C = −40.

Convection as a mode of heat transfer occurs in:
topics.explanation: Convection requires fluid flow and occurs in liquids and gases, not solids or vacuum.

topics.q: A thermometer uses mercury because mercury:
options: Has uniform thermal expansion and is visible
topics.explanation: Mercury has uniform expansion, high boiling point, low freezing point and is easily visible.

topics.q: An ideal gas undergoes isothermal expansion. The internal energy:
topics.explanation: For an ideal gas, internal energy depends only on temperature. In isothermal process, T is constant, so U is unchanged.

topics.q: The Stefan-Boltzmann law states that radiated power is proportional to:
topics.explanation: Stefan-Boltzmann Law: P = σAT⁴; power radiated is proportional to the fourth power of absolute temperature.

Heat flows from a hot body to a cold body until:
topics.explanation: Heat transfer continues until both bodies reach the same temperature — thermal equilibrium.

topics.q: Which of the following processes is adiabatic?
options: Boiling water in an open container
Rapid expansion of gas in insulated cylinder
Slow heating on a hot plate
topics.explanation: An adiabatic process involves no heat exchange with surroundings, like rapid expansion in an insulated container.

topics.q: The zeroth law of thermodynamics defines:
topics.explanation: The zeroth law establishes that temperature is a well-defined quantity through the concept of thermal equilibrium.

topics.q: Greenhouse effect on Earth is caused primarily by:
options: CO₂ and water vapour trapping infrared radiation
topics.explanation: Greenhouse gases like CO₂ and H₂O absorb and re-emit infrared radiation, trapping heat near Earth's surface.

topics.q: Entropy of the universe in any natural process:
topics.explanation: Second Law of Thermodynamics: Total entropy of an isolated system always increases for irreversible processes.

topics.q: Which law of thermodynamics introduces the concept of entropy?
topics.explanation: The Second Law of thermodynamics introduces entropy and states it increases in irreversible processes.

topics.q: At absolute zero (0 K), the entropy of a perfect crystal is:
topics.explanation: Third Law of Thermodynamics: Entropy of a perfect crystal approaches zero at absolute zero.

topics.q: The process in which pressure remains constant is called:
topics.explanation: Isobaric process: pressure is constant. Isothermal: temp constant. Isochoric: volume constant.

topics.q: When water is cooled from 4°C to 0°C, its density:
topics.explanation: Water has anomalous expansion — density is maximum at 4°C and decreases from 4°C to 0°C.

topics.q: The black body radiation spectrum was correctly explained by:
topics.explanation: Max Planck explained blackbody radiation by proposing energy quantization (E=hν).

magnetism.q: The SI unit of magnetic field strength (B) is:
magnetism.explanation: Tesla (T) is the SI unit of magnetic field strength (also called magnetic flux density). 1 Tesla = 1 Wb/m².

magnetism.q: Electromagnetic induction was discovered by:
magnetism.explanation: Michael Faraday discovered electromagnetic induction in 1831. A changing magnetic field induces an EMF in a conductor.

magnetism.q: Lenz's Law states that the induced current:
options: Is always in the same direction as flux
magnetism.explanation: Lenz's Law: Induced current opposes the change in magnetic flux that produces it. This is consistent with conservation of energy.

magnetism.q: A cyclotron is used to:
options: Accelerate charged particles to high speeds
magnetism.explanation: A cyclotron uses electric and magnetic fields to accelerate charged particles (protons, deuterons) to high speeds for nuclear physics experiments.

magnetism.q: The SI unit of magnetic flux is:
magnetism.explanation: Magnetic flux Φ = B·A is measured in Weber (Wb). 1 Wb = 1 T·m². Tesla is the unit of magnetic field strength B.

magnetism.q: A current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field experiences a force. This is the principle of:
magnetism.explanation: Electric motor converts electrical energy to mechanical energy using the force on current-carrying conductor in magnetic field (F = BIL).

magnetism.q: According to Fleming's Left Hand Rule, the thumb points in the direction of:
magnetism.explanation: Fleming's LHR: Forefinger=Field, Middle finger=Current, Thumb=Force (motion). Used for motors.

magnetism.q: Magnetic field lines always:
magnetism.explanation: Magnetic field lines form closed continuous loops — outside magnet from N to S, inside magnet from S to N. They never start or end (unlike electric field lines).

magnetism.q: Transformer works on the principle of:
magnetism.explanation: Transformer uses mutual inductance — changing current in primary coil induces EMF in secondary coil through shared magnetic flux.

magnetism.q: A step-up transformer has 100 turns in primary and 1000 turns in secondary. If primary voltage is 220V, secondary voltage is:
magnetism.explanation: Vs/Vp = Ns/Np → Vs = 220 × (1000/100) = 2200 V. More turns in secondary = step up in voltage.

magnetism.q: Earth's magnetic field is due to:
options: Convective currents in liquid outer core
magnetism.explanation: Earth's magnetic field is generated by electric currents in the molten liquid outer core (geodynamo theory), not a permanent magnet.

magnetism.q: Which of the following materials is ferromagnetic?
magnetism.explanation: Iron, cobalt, and nickel are ferromagnetic — they are strongly attracted to magnets and can be permanently magnetised.

magnetism.q: Fleming's Right Hand Rule is used to find the direction of:
magnetism.explanation: Fleming's RHR: Forefinger=Field, Thumb=Motion, Middle finger=Induced current. Used for generators (opposite of LHR which is for motors).

magnetism.q: The magnetic field inside a solenoid is:
magnetism.explanation: Inside a long solenoid, the magnetic field is uniform (constant magnitude) and directed parallel to the axis of the solenoid.

magnetism.q: Magnetic declination at a place is the angle between:
options: Horizontal and vertical component of Earth's field
magnetism.explanation: Magnetic declination = angle between true geographic north and magnetic north (compass direction). Dip/inclination is the angle with horizontal.

magnetism.q: The force on a charge q moving with velocity v in magnetic field B at angle θ is:
magnetism.explanation: Lorentz magnetic force F = qvBsinθ, where θ is angle between v and B.

magnetism.q: A current-carrying solenoid behaves like:
magnetism.explanation: A current-carrying solenoid behaves like a bar magnet with a north and south pole.

magnetism.q: The SI unit of inductance is:
magnetism.explanation: Henry (H) is the SI unit of inductance.

magnetism.q: According to Ampere's circuital law, the magnetic field along a closed path is related to:
magnetism.explanation: Ampere's law: ∮B·dl = μ₀I, relating magnetic field to the enclosed current.

magnetism.q: The magnetic susceptibility of a diamagnetic material is:
magnetism.explanation: Diamagnetic materials have small negative susceptibility — they are weakly repelled by magnets.

magnetism.q: An AC generator works on the principle of:
magnetism.explanation: AC generator converts mechanical energy to electrical energy using electromagnetic induction (Faraday's law).

magnetism.q: The strength of an electromagnet can be increased by:
options: Using iron core and increasing current
magnetism.explanation: Electromagnet strength increases with current, number of turns, and using a ferromagnetic (iron) core.

magnetism.q: In an ideal transformer, if the secondary coil has twice the turns of the primary, the secondary voltage is:
magnetism.explanation: V₂/V₁ = N₂/N₁ = 2. Secondary voltage is twice the primary.

magnetism.q: The period of revolution of a charged particle in a uniform magnetic field:
magnetism.explanation: T = 2πm/(qB); the period depends on mass, charge and B — independent of speed.

magnetism.q: Magnetic field lines inside a bar magnet go from:
magnetism.explanation: Inside a magnet, field lines go from south to north (completing the loop that runs N to S outside).

magnetism.q: The phenomenon of electromagnetic induction was discovered by:
magnetism.explanation: Michael Faraday discovered electromagnetic induction in 1831.

magnetism.q: Retentivity of a magnet refers to:
options: The residual magnetism after removing the magnetising field
The coercive force required to demagnetise
magnetism.explanation: Retentivity is the residual magnetic flux density remaining after the magnetising force is removed.

magnetism.q: In a DC motor, the commutator's function is to:
options: Reverse current direction every half revolution
magnetism.explanation: The commutator reverses the current direction in the armature every half turn, maintaining unidirectional rotation.

magnetism.q: A proton and an electron moving with the same velocity enter a magnetic field perpendicularly. The radius of proton's path compared to electron is:
magnetism.explanation: r = mv/(qB). Proton has much greater mass than electron (same q), so its radius is much larger.

magnetism.q: The angle of dip at the equator is:
magnetism.explanation: At the magnetic equator, the Earth's field is horizontal; the dip (inclination) is 0°.

magnetism.q: Soft iron is preferred for making electromagnets because it has:
magnetism.explanation: Soft iron has low retentivity (easily demagnetised) and low coercivity (easy to magnetise/demagnetise).

magnetism.q: A charged particle moves parallel to a magnetic field. The force on it is:
magnetism.explanation: F=qvBsinθ. When θ=0° (parallel), F=qvBsin0°=0.

magnetism.q: The phenomenon responsible for energy losses in transformer cores is:
magnetism.explanation: Hysteresis loss occurs in transformer cores when the magnetic domain orientation cycles repeatedly.

magnetism.q: Diamagnetic materials placed in a non-uniform magnetic field will:
magnetism.explanation: Diamagnets are weakly repelled by magnetic fields; they move toward the weaker region.

magnetism.q: The working principle of a galvanometer is based on:
options: Torque on current-carrying coil in magnetic field
magnetism.explanation: A galvanometer works on the torque (τ=NIAB) experienced by a current-carrying coil in a magnetic field.

magnetism.q: A 200-turn coil of area 0.01 m² is in a 0.5 T field. Flux through the coil when perpendicular to field is:
magnetism.explanation: Flux Φ = NBAcosθ = 200×0.5×0.01×cos0° = 1 Wb.

magnetism.q: An electron (m=9.1×10⁻³¹ kg, q=1.6×10⁻¹⁹ C) moves at 10⁶ m/s in a 0.1 T field. Radius of circular path is:
A transformer has 500 primary turns and 50 secondary turns. If primary current is 2A, secondary current is:
magnetism.explanation: I₂/I₁=N₁/N₂=500/50=10. I₂=10×2=20 A (step-down transformer).

magnetism.q: The EMF induced in a coil of 100 turns when flux changes from 0.02 Wb to 0.06 Wb in 0.2 s is:
A long straight wire carries 10 A. Magnetic field at 5 cm distance is: (μ₀=4π×10⁻⁷ T·m/A)
The magnetic moment of a bar magnet is M. If it is bent into a semicircle, the new magnetic moment is:
magnetism.explanation: If L is original length, bent into semicircle: πr=L → r=L/π. New moment = m×2r = m×2L/π = 2M/π.

magnetism.q: Two bar magnets are placed with their like poles facing each other. The resultant magnetic field at the midpoint between them is:
magnetism.explanation: Like poles facing each other produce fields in opposite directions at the midpoint, which cancel out.

magnetism.q: A compass needle placed at the magnetic equator points:
magnetism.explanation: At the magnetic equator, the field is horizontal. The compass needle aligns with the horizontal component — geographic North-South differs. Needle points along horizontal magnetic field direction.

magnetism.q: The time period of a magnetic needle oscillating in Earth's horizontal field is T. If horizontal field is doubled, new period is:
magnetism.explanation: T=2π√(I/MH). Doubling H: T'=2π√(I/2MH)=T/√2.

magnetism.q: A current of 2A flows through a circular coil of 100 turns and radius 5 cm. Magnetic field at centre is: (μ₀=4π×10⁻⁷ T·m/A)
A straight wire of length 0.5 m carrying 10 A is placed at 30° to a uniform field of 0.1 T. Force on the wire is:
An EMF of 50V is induced in a coil when current changes from 0 to 5A in 0.1 s. Self-inductance of the coil is:
A rectangular coil 10 cm × 5 cm of 50 turns carries 2A in a 0.3 T field. Maximum torque on coil is:
In a transformer, if primary is 240V with 400 turns and secondary has 100 turns, the secondary current when 4A primary current flows is:
magnetism.explanation: Power conservation: V₁I₁=V₂I₂. V₂=240×100/400=60V. I₂=V₁I₁/V₂=240×4/60=16 A.
